title: AWS CEO Matt Garman says data centers aren’t using as much water as claimed; debunks 4 ‘popular myths’; s
key_facts: AWS CEO Matt Garman said in a blog post that AWS has stopped using nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) with government agencies on data center projects.
He said more than 100 data center moratoriums are being considered across the US and warned of a 'losing ticket' in the AI race.
He argued four myths: water, electricity costs, pollution and community benefits.
He said direct data center water use is 0.5% of US industrial water use.
He said generators run about 10 hours a year, idle 99.9% of the time.
TechCrunch notes the claims are Amazon's own; critics say they ignore water used for power and chips, and a watchdog blamed data centers for a 76% year-on-year price rise on America's largest grid.
quote_evidence: Amazon Web Services CEO Matt Garman said the company has stopped using nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) in its dealings with government agencies as it seeks approval to build new data centers.
“The truth is data center generators almost never run,” Garman said.
why_it_matters_hint: Amazon is publicly rebutting data center criticism and dropping NDAs as moratorium pressure grows.
notes: Times of India page returned no text; the story was read at TechCrunch (3 Oct 2026). The Times of India article is the pool item (5 Oct).
